correctness.rationale: The final claim is vertex-anchored. The six boundary points are explicit in \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)\), and each normalized consecutive side vector is exactly a vertex or edge point of the difference body \(D=(C-C)/2\), proving common relative side length \(3(\sqrt5-1)/4\). The inspected primary theorem states that for \(k\ge4\), relatively equilateral \(k\)-gons with a common prescribed boundary vertex have the same side length. Exact symbolic replay verifies every displayed identity. No global optimization or finite experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: The regular pentagon is singled out in the primary source as the likely extremal body for six-point homothetic packing, and its pictured configuration is given only approximately. Prescribing a vertex is mathematically canonical rather than arbitrary because the source proves that every relatively equilateral hexagon through that vertex has the same side length. The exact value therefore supplies a natural reproducible benchmark for the unresolved global problem and converts a published decimal picture into a closed structural invariant.
